Forms of address: du or Sie

Source: R/data.R
address_forms.Rd

Whether German speakers address a stranger with informal du or formal Sie, by speaker age group and setting. 30 speakers per cell, one observation each. For contingency tables and chi-squared tests.

Usage

address_forms

Format

A tibble with 180 rows and 4 columns:

speaker

Speaker ID, S001 to S180.

age_group

"under 30" or "over 50".

setting

"university", "office" or "shop".

form

"Sie" or "du".

Source

data-raw/address_forms.R

Details

True model: the probability of du is 0.85 (university), 0.35 (shop) and 0.45 (office) for speakers under 30, and 0.40, 0.08 and 0.15 for speakers over 50. These probabilities are simulated. Strangers are by default addressed with Sie, and variation in address depends more on age than on region (Kretzenbacher 2011). In a 2021 survey reported by Kretzenbacher and Hensel-Börner (2024), 44% of customers aged 18 to 29 liked being addressed with du in shops, against 23% of those aged 60 and over.

References

Kretzenbacher, H. L. (2011). Perceptions of national and regional standards of addressing in Germany and Austria. Pragmatics, 21(1), 69-83. doi:10.1075/prag.21.1.04kre

Kretzenbacher, H. L. & Hensel-Börner, S. (2024). Pronominal address in German sales talk: Effects on the perception of the salesperson. Languages, 9(10), 316. doi:10.3390/languages9100316

Examples

tab <- xtabs(~ setting + form + age_group, data = address_forms)
round(prop.table(tab, c(1, 3))[, "du", ], 2)
#>             age_group
#> setting      under 30 over 50
#>   university     0.83    0.47
#>   office         0.47    0.17
#>   shop           0.33    0.10
chisq.test(tab[, , "under 30"])
#> 
#> 	Pearson's Chi-squared test
#> 
#> data:  tab[, , "under 30"]
#> X-squared = 16.217, df = 2, p-value = 0.000301
#> 
chisq.test(tab[, , "over 50"])
#> 
#> 	Pearson's Chi-squared test
#> 
#> data:  tab[, , "over 50"]
#> X-squared = 12.393, df = 2, p-value = 0.002036
#>
